cards.text: Right before this, the LORD warned Judah that a distant nation was coming, because they had forsaken Him (Jer 5:15, 19). Now He has more to say, and it goes out to the house of Jacob and to Judah. Declare it AND proclaim it, friend, which means this is not a whisper, this is every rooftop on the street.

cards.question: The LORD opens by calling His people foolish and senseless. They've got eyes and ears. So what's the trouble with them?

answers.text: Their eyes don't see and their ears don't hear
They see and hear but forget it all fast
They see and hear but never speak up

cards.text: Eyes that don't see, ears that don't hear... that's me staring RIGHT at a beeping oven timer and still burning the whole batch. Then the LORD asks them, 'Do you not fear Me?'

cards.question: The LORD reminds His people who they're dealing with: the One who set a boundary for the sea. What did He set as that boundary?
The waves surge and roar against the boundary the LORD set for the sea, and sometimes they break right through it.
The sea stays right where the LORD put it. But what does He say about the hearts of His people?

cards.text: They've turned aside and gone away. And there's one thing they never said in their hearts: 'Let us fear the LORD our God…'

cards.question: The LORD is the God who keeps the appointed weeks of harvest, the One who gives the ___ in season, both autumn and spring.

cards.text: God sends the rains and keeps the harvest coming, and nobody stops to fear Him, which is like eating every cookie in the box and never ONCE wondering who baked them. Now the LORD says something has diverted those gifts away from them.

cards.question: The LORD says it's His people's own iniquities and sins that have kept His bounty from them.

cards.text: Now the LORD gets specific. Among His people are wicked men, and they watch like fowlers lying in wait.

cards.question: These wicked men lie in wait like bird catchers. But what do they set a trap to catch?

cards.text: Picture a bird catcher's cages, packed full of birds. The LORD says that's what these men's houses look like.

cards.question: Like cages full of birds, the houses of these wicked men are full of ___.
All that deceit has left these wicked men poor and weak.

cards.text: Powerful, rich, fat AND sleek. They're trapping people like birds, and somehow they've got the SHINIEST houses on the whole block.

cards.question: These rich men have excelled in the deeds of the wicked. Whose cause have they not taken up?

cards.text: They haven't defended the rights of the needy either. So the LORD asks the same question He asked earlier in this chapter (Jer 5:9): 'Should I not punish them for these things?'
Then He says a horrible and shocking thing has happened in the land. Friend, when the One who holds back the sea with sand calls something shocking, you put the cookie DOWN and you listen.

cards.question: The horrible and shocking thing in the land starts with the prophets. What are they doing?
And it doesn't stop with the prophets. The priests rule by their own ___.
The LORD's people are upset about these prophets and priests and want things to change.

cards.text: Nope. My people love it so, the LORD says, and then He leaves them with one last question: 'but what will you do in the end?'

findings.problem: The opening card says the LORD 'warned Judah that a distant nation was coming' and cites Jer 5:15. In the BSB, Jer 5:15 is addressed to 'O house of Israel', not Judah. The card renames who the warning was spoken to.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Jer 5:27 compares the fullness of the houses: 'Like cages full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit.' The card turns this into a comparison of appearance: 'The LORD says that's what these men's houses look like.' The text never says the houses look like cages. It says they are full the way cages are full.

The card says 'They're trapping people like birds, and somehow they've got the SHINIEST houses on the whole block.' Jer 5:27 gives the cause directly: 'Therefore they have become powerful and rich.' Saying 'somehow' presents their wealth as unexplained, which the text shows is not so. The joke is also flat, and the 'shiny houses' detail sounds like a Bible fact rather than a clear joke.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The blank 'The priests rule by their own ___' with the options authority, tribe and wealth asks the baker to guess wording, not reason out meaning. Nothing on the earlier cards points to 'authority' over 'wealth'. In fact, 'wealth' echoes the earlier card about the wicked growing rich, and 'tribe' is plausible for priests. A thoughtful baker can only guess.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
